title: Papers of the day, 20 November 2026
summary: The 10 arXiv papers of 20 November 2026 closest to what this site covers: VideoRNG; Keel; ARISE; T/E/S structural representation for LLM reasoning dynamics; RecurrentVLM; Parametric memory management for LLMs (fixed-capacity LoRA memory substrate); SceneAnything; Introspective Oversight; Software thermodynamics theory for agentic coding; RFBench.
research_notes:
1. VideoRNG introduced for relightable 3D asset generation from video models. Researchers announced VideoRNG, a two-stage generative method that produces relightable 3D assets from a text prompt or single image. It uses a fine-tuned video diffusion model to create turntable RGBA sequences, then a large reconstruction model that maps video latents to millions of anisotropic Gaussians with neural appearance features, rendered via ray-traced rtRNG.
2. Keel introduced as agentic weight-editing method for VLM reasoning loops. On 2026-11-20 an arXiv preprint (2611.25257) introduced Keel, the first agentic weight-editing method for vision-language models on image tasks. A frontier multimodal LLM acts as an agent to locate and remove reasoning loops in Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-2B by editing weights, without training and while keeping model size and per-token cost. The preprint reports fewer loops, shorter answers, and higher accuracy than thinking-mode baselines across six image benchmarks.
3. ARISE self-evolving memory architecture for enterprise LLM agents. An arXiv preprint (2611.23588) introduces ARISE, a memory architecture in which enterprise LLM agents refine their memory from their own failures without updating weights, tools, or workflow logic. Reported results across 14 enterprise-workflow domains on SOP-Bench and tau^2-bench show accuracy gains over baseline and over GEPA, with lower model-call and output-token counts.
4. T/E/S structural representation models LLM reasoning dynamics. An arXiv preprint (2611.23749v1, announced 2026-11-20) proposes T/E/S, a structural representation combining text, local events, and activity spans to predict next outcomes in LLM reasoning. Reported results include improved prediction in most evaluation groups for a Transformer and Qwen with LoRA, reduced CPU inference time in finite-process experiments, and a lower Brier loss for a compact observer on HotpotQA and MuSiQue questions. The paper also notes annotation errors in the observer.
5. RecurrentVLM introduced for recurrent video object tracking in vision language models. A new arXiv paper proposes RecurrentVLM, which makes each attention layer of a pretrained vision language model recur over time by computing keys and values from finished frame groups. The authors report 100% on VET-Bench, 99.6% on MET-Bench, and 99% on 50-swap shell games after training on at most 30 swaps. Code is stated to be forthcoming.
6. New arXiv paper proposes parametric memory management with decaying LoRA adapter for LLMs. An arXiv preprint (2611.25235, published 2026-11-20) proposes a system for managing user memory directly in LLM weights, using a fixed-capacity LoRA adapter with k-hot rank combinations, independently controlled temporal decay, and a learned controller policy. The authors report achieving 86% of oracle performance on a new long-horizon user-memory evaluation dataset.
7. SceneAnything: agentic reconstruction of mesh scenes from a single video. An arXiv preprint (2611.25340) introduces SceneAnything, an automated agent-based system that reconstructs editable Blender mesh scenes from real or generated videos, using pretrained vision models, a scene-owner agent, and reusable programs. The authors report improved original-view fidelity over direct-agent reconstruction and higher novel-view similarity than compared video-to-3D methods on 100 scenes, and plan to release the harness and scenes.
8. Introspective oversight method trains language models to answer questions about their own behavior. An arXiv preprint published 2026-11-20 proposes introspective oversight, which trains a separate third-person observer role in a language model to answer questions about the assistant's behavior, verified against actual behavior. Reported results on five held-out oversight evaluations include a mean AUROC of 0.907 for an observer trained on Qwen3.6-27B, compared with 0.864 for honesty training, 0.828 for transcript monitoring, and 0.796 for activation oracles.
9. arXiv paper proposes software thermodynamics theory for agentic coding token costs. An arXiv preprint dated 2026-11-20 introduces a theory of software thermodynamics for coding agents, treating generated tokens as cost split into work and heat, with the test suite as a Maxwell's daemon. The authors report that about 80 percent of tokens in successful runs are heat, a free energy estimate of 14 to 22 percent of mean run cost, and coding costing 1.1 to 1.5 times uncoding.
10. RFBench multimodal benchmark for passive RF layout design released on arXiv. Researchers announced RFBench (arXiv:2611.23410), a simulator-grounded dataset and benchmark of 10,000 two-port planar RF layouts for evaluating multimodal language models on layout generation, response prediction, and related tasks. The preprint reports that RF-specific fine-tuning raised structural validity from 0.0% to 83.2% on one task.
